name: HippoRAG 2

paper.title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models

construction.unit: passage node + phrase nodes from the passage's OpenIE triples
construction.kept_as: passages verbatim; LLM-extracted (subject, predicate, object) triples as an index
construction.processing: LLM NER, then NER-conditioned triple extraction per passage; phrases, triples and passages embedded; synonym edges for phrase pairs with similarity >= 0.8

organization.structure: open knowledge graph: phrase nodes and passage nodes; relation, synonym and 'contains' edges
organization.stores: igraph KG + three embedding stores (passages, phrases, triples)
organization.index: NV-Embed-v2 dense over passages and triple strings; phrase embeddings only for synonym edges

management.operations: new passages add nodes and edges (corpus-expansion test in §6.3); code also has a delete call

retrieval.query: question embedded twice (query-to-triple and query-to-passage instructions)
retrieval.candidates: top-5 triples by dense similarity; dense scores for every passage
retrieval.selection: LLM filter keeps <= 4 triples; Personalized PageRank seeded by <= 5 phrases and all passages (x 0.05); passages ranked by PageRank

use.context: top-5 passages as 'Wikipedia Title: ...' blocks after a one-shot example

classify.note: Dense triple matching and the LLM filter only set the PPR seeds; the PageRank ranking over the whole graph decides the 5 passages.

stages.ingestion: The corpus is a fixed set of passages (e.g. 11,656 for MuSiQue); each passage becomes a node as is.
stages.construction: An LLM runs NER on each passage and then extracts schema-free (subject, predicate, object) triples conditioned on those entities; subjects and objects become phrase nodes.
stages.organization: Phrase nodes are joined by relation edges (same triple) and synonym edges (embedding similarity >= 0.8); each passage node gets a 'contains' edge to every phrase from its triples.
stages.update: New passages are indexed into the same graph (the paper grows the corpus in four segments, §6.3); nothing is edited or merged beyond synonym links.
stages.retrieval: The question is matched to triple embeddings (top 5), an LLM keeps the relevant ones (at most 4), and their phrases (up to 5) plus every passage (dense score x 0.05) seed Personalized PageRank; passages are ranked by PageRank. With no triples left, plain dense retrieval is used.
stages.answer: The reader LLM gets the top 5 passages and answers after a short chain of thought.

summary: Adds passages as nodes to HippoRAG's LLM-built phrase graph, links the question to whole triples, and filters those triples with an LLM before Personalized PageRank ranks passages.

headline: The reader only ever sees 5 raw passages; triples and phrases decide the ranking but never reach the answer model.
Every passage is a PageRank seed weighted by its dense score (x 0.05), so the dense retriever still anchors the result; phrase seeds come from at most 5 phrases in LLM-kept triples.
If the LLM filter keeps no triple, the graph is skipped and plain dense retrieval answers (18 of 100 failure cases in App. E).

fields.what: embedded as the string of the tuple; matched to the question and read by the filter LLM

fields.name: predicate on the graph

fields.name: relation edge
fields.what: subject-object pair from a triple, weight = number of times seen

fields.name: synonym edge
fields.what: phrase pair with embedding similarity >= 0.8, weight = similarity

fields.name: context edge
fields.what: passage 'contains' each phrase of its triples, weight 1.0

answer_context.format: system prompt + one-shot example, then "Wikipedia Title: {passage}" x5, "Question: {q}" and "Thought: "; the answer is taken after "Answer:"

answer_context.note: The same QA prompt is used to re-phrase GraphRAG and LightRAG outputs (App. G.2).

compression.basis: Not reported; passages are stored and read verbatim, so no text is shortened.

paper_vs_code.paper: average score of the filtered triples the phrase appears in
paper_vs_code.code: score of the last kept triple containing the phrase (the average only picks the top 5); changed to an average in 242abfb (2025-06-24)

paper_vs_code.paper: phrase nodes take their ranking score directly as reset probability
paper_vs_code.code: the score is divided by the number of passages that contain the phrase (kept after the 2025-06 change)

open_questions: 'w/o Passage Node' removes the passage nodes and the dense passage seeds together, so the ablation cannot say whether the graph edges or simply mixing dense scores into the ranking carry the gain.
No run replaces PageRank with a direct rerank of dense results by the kept triples' phrases, so how much the graph walk adds beyond recognition is not measured.
The dense passage weight is set on MuSiQue and NQ dev sets (Table 5) and then used for all benchmarks.

glance.a: A passage, kept whole as a graph node, plus the (subject, predicate, object) triples an LLM extracted from it; their subjects and objects become phrase nodes.
No. Passages are stored and read verbatim; triples are only an index for linking the question to the graph.
One open knowledge graph: phrase nodes joined by triple edges and synonym edges (similarity >= 0.8), and a 'contains' edge from each passage to its phrases.
An LLM filters the 5 best-matching triples down to at most 4, and Personalized PageRank then re-orders all passages. There is no cross-encoder.

glance.q: Is memory reconstructed at question time?
glance.a: No second round. If the filter keeps no triple, the system falls back to plain dense passage retrieval.

glance.q: What does the answer model read?
glance.a: The top 5 passages as 'Wikipedia Title: ...' blocks after a one-shot example, then the question.

discussion.takeaway: Putting passages into HippoRAG's graph and linking the question to whole triples lets a PageRank retriever keep its multi-hop gains without losing to a strong 7B dense retriever on simple QA: 59.8 vs 57.0 average F1.

claims.claim: Earlier structure-augmented RAG falls below strong dense retrieval once simple factual QA is included; HippoRAG 2 does not.
claims.evidence: Average F1: NV-Embed-v2 57.0, RAPTOR 48.8, GraphRAG 49.6, LightRAG 6.6, HippoRAG 53.1, HippoRAG 2 59.8; NQ 63.3 vs 61.9. Table 2, §5

claims.claim: The largest gains are on associative (multi-hop) tasks.
claims.evidence: 2Wiki F1 71.0 vs 61.5, LV-Eval 12.9 vs 9.8; recall@5 MuSiQue 74.7 vs 69.7, 2Wiki 90.4 vs 76.5. Tables 2-3

claims.claim: Each design change helps, linking the question to triples most of all.
claims.evidence: Recall@5 average 87.1 vs 74.6 with NER-to-node, 59.6 with query-to-node, 81.0 without passage nodes, 86.4 without the filter. Table 4, §6.1

claims.claim: The gain holds with other dense retrievers.
Indexing is far cheaper than GraphRAG or LightRAG.
claims.evidence: MuSiQue: 9.2M input tokens vs 115.5M (GraphRAG) and 68.5M (LightRAG); 1.2 s per query vs 10.7 s and 13.3 s. Table 12, App. F

limits: The triple filter is a main error source: in 26% of 100 failed MuSiQue questions no supporting phrase survives filtering, and 18% end with no triple at all.
Graph search can still miss supporting passages when the right phrases are linked.
QA needs more GPU memory than the baselines (9.9 GB vs 1.7 GB for NV-Embed-v2) because of the fact embeddings.
Associative QA degrades as the corpus grows, at about the same rate as dense retrieval.
Episodic memory for long conversations is left for future work.
discussion.limits_src: paper App. E, App. F, §6.3, §7 (no separate limitations section)
reading: The reader always gets 5 verbatim passages; the graph only re-orders them, so HippoRAG 2 is best read as a graph-based reranker over a passage corpus rather than a store the model reads from.
Every passage is a PageRank seed with its dense score, so dense retrieval stays in the loop; Table 5 shows the result is sensitive to that weight (MuSiQue recall@5 77.9 to 80.5).

The abstract's 7% associativity gain matches recall@5 averaged over MuSiQue, 2Wiki and HotpotQA (87.1 vs 80.2); in QA F1 the average gain over NV-Embed-v2 on the four multi-hop sets is about 4 points, and on HotpotQA it is 0.2.
At the pinned commit a phrase's seed weight is the last kept triple's score divided by how many passages contain the phrase; the paper describes an average, and the division is not described.

GraphRAG and LightRAG answers are re-phrased with HippoRAG's QA prompt (App. G.2), and LightRAG averages 6.6 F1 with Llama (13.9 with GPT-4o-mini), so part of the gap to these baselines reflects how they were ported.
LV-Eval (124 questions) and NarrativeQA (293 questions over 10 documents) are small samples; the other five sets use 1,000 sampled questions each.
Continual learning is tested only by adding corpus segments (Fig. 3); no experiment updates or corrects stored facts.

abstract.text: HippoRAG 2 treats retrieval-augmented generation as non-parametric continual learning and asks whether structure-augmented RAG can match strong dense retrievers on simple factual questions while keeping its advantage on multi-hop and long-narrative ones. It keeps HippoRAG's LLM-built open knowledge graph and Personalized PageRank search, but adds the passages themselves as graph nodes, links the whole question to triples instead of to extracted entities, and lets an LLM filter those triples before they seed the search. On seven QA benchmarks it reports the best average F1 against large embedding models and graph- or summary-based RAG, with the largest gains on multi-hop sets.
